title: Triad SDK credential simplifier and stream-flow parity (ergonomics & retry harmonization)
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: SDK consumers across Python/TypeScript/Go reported friction when configuring credential refresh, retry presets, and stream cancellation semantics. This PR introduces a compact, consistent credential surface and harmonizes retry profiles + stream flow semantics across all three SDKs so application code can be ported with minimal changes.

Summary of changes: consolidated 'CredentialProvider' API shape, introduced a lightweight 'CredHint' for prefetching, aligned retry defaults (idempotent vs. non-idempotent) and added a small stream-control API that exposes cancelable checkpoints for long-running pull-streams. The change is intentionally additive: it builds atop existing adapters and provides compatibility shims for older consumer code.

Per-SDK highlights: Python: new redwood_sdk.cred.CompactProvider and CredHint ctx-manager; retry presets exposed as RetryProfile enum; stream.PullStream gains .checkpoint() and .cancel_checkpoint(token) helpers. TypeScript: exported CredentialSimplifier, light-weight async iterator helpers (checkpoint / cancel), and minor ergonomic wrappers for common credential configs. Go: introduced cred.Simplifier interface, prefetch helper, and a StreamCheckpoint token returned from Stream.NextCheckpoint().

Testing and rollout: unit + integration test matrix added for all SDKs. E2E matrix ran against staging runtime and Dedicated local canary. Backwards compatibility shim added so existing token providers still work; deprecation warnings are logged (non-fatal) for legacy constructor signatures. Rollout plan is staged: merge to main, cut patch SDK releases (py 2.2.0, ts 1.9.0, go 1.5.0) and coordinate changelogs.

Notes: this PR intentionally does not change server-side behavior; it is an SDK ergonomics and parity patch. We coordinated with the docs team for migration guidance and added short examples to each SDK README.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Overall this looks great — thanks for the cross-sdk coordination. Two small asks: add a short example for using checkpoint in serverless cold-start scenarios, and confirm the impact on connection lifetimes for long polls.
Priya Nair: Added serverless example in docs and updated TS quickstart. Long poll behavior unchanged by default; checkpoint tokens don't keep separate TCP connections alive — noted in docs.
Luca Fernandez: Can we tighten the RetryProfile default for non-idempotent calls to avoid accidental retries? Suggest non-idempotent default = no auto-retry, only on explicit opt-in.
Priya Nair: Agree — changed default mapping so non-idempotent = opt-in retries; opened follow-up ENG-2009 to audit existing client configs.
Marcel Dupont: Integration tests flaked once on macOS matrix; looks like a timing var in pullstream checkpoint — added small backoff and stable test assertion.
Priya Nair: Re-ran macOS job and tests are stable. CI green.
Ethan Park: Approving after test fix. Ready to merge once changelogs are polished.
Luca Fernandez: Approved. Noting there will be a minor SDK version bump coordination call post-merge.
release_notes: SDK ergonomics: Introduce compact credential APIs across Python/TypeScript/Go to simplify credential prefetch and refresh
Streaming: Add checkpoint() and cancel_checkpoint() helpers to pull-streams to improve long-poll ergonomics
Retries: Align retry defaults; non-idempotent calls now opt-in for automatic retries
Backward compatibility: Legacy credential providers continue to work via a shim; deprecation warnings added
